## Code Review: `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/review_target.py`

### Critical (blocks merge)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 1 | review_target.py:11 | Security — SQL injection | Coding-standards §3.2 (validate at boundaries) / OWASP Top 10 | `order_id` is interpolated directly into a SQL string via an f-string (`f"SELECT total FROM orders WHERE id = {order_id}"`). Any caller passing an unsanitized `order_id` can inject arbitrary SQL. | Use a parameterized query: `db_conn.execute("SELECT total FROM orders WHERE id = ?", (order_id,))` (or the driver's placeholder syntax). |
| 2 | review_target.py:24 | Security — SQL injection | Coding-standards §3.2 | Same f-string injection pattern reused in the `UPDATE` statement. | Parameterize: `db_conn.execute("UPDATE orders SET status='paid' WHERE id = ?", (order_id,))`. |
| 3 | review_target.py:19-22 | Anti-pattern — swallowed error / silent failure | Coding-standards §9 ("Catching / swallowing errors 'just in case' without a named failure mode") | A failed payment (`resp.status_code != 200`) returns `None` with no exception, no log, no distinguishable failure mode. The caller cannot tell "no discount" apart from "payment failed," and the order is left in an inconsistent state (charge attempted, DB not updated, no record of the failure). | Raise a named exception (e.g. `PaymentFailedError(order_id, resp.status_code)`) or return a typed `Result`/status object the caller must handle explicitly. |

### Important (should fix before merge)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 4 | review_target.py:8-25 | SOLID — SRP | Coding-standards §1.1 | `process_order` does four unrelated things: reads from the DB, computes a discount, performs an HTTP payment call, and writes back to the DB. Describing it requires "and" repeatedly — the SRP litmus test in §1.1 fails. Two independent stakeholders (pricing rules vs. payment integration) would need to change this same function. | Split into `get_order_total(db_conn, order_id)`, `apply_discount(total)` (pure function, core/domain), and `charge_and_mark_paid(order_id, total, db_conn, payment_gateway)` (orchestration/infrastructure), composed by a use-case function. |
| 5 | review_target.py:13 | Magic number | Coding-standards §3.1 / §8 (no invented constants) | `500` (discount threshold) and `0.9` (10% discount multiplier) are unexplained numeric literals with no name and no `# source:` citation. | Extract named constants, e.g. `BULK_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD = 500` and `BULK_DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER = 0.9`, each with a `# source:` comment pointing to the pricing policy/spec that defines them. |
| 6 | review_target.py:8, 18 | Clean Architecture — DIP / layering | Coding-standards §2.2, §5.1 | The function takes a concrete `db_conn` and directly imports/calls `requests` (a concrete infrastructure library) inline. There is no abstraction (`PaymentGateway`, `OrderRepository` protocol) for business logic to depend on — core logic and infrastructure detail are fused. | Define `PaymentGateway` and `OrderRepository` protocols in the core layer; inject concrete implementations (`StripePaymentGateway`, `SqlOrderRepository`) from a composition root. `process_order` (or its replacement use case) should depend only on the protocols. |
| 7 | review_target.py:8 | Reliability — missing types | Coding-standards §3.2 ("Use the language's type system fully") | `order_id`, `db_conn` have no type annotations; the function has no return type annotation (implicit `Optional[float] | None`, but that's never stated). | Add type hints: `def process_order(order_id: int, db_conn: DBConnection) -> Decimal: ...` (with the DB/payment types being the protocols from #6). |

### Minor (optional, improve later)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 8 | review_target.py:12 | Reliability — no boundary validation | Coding-standards §3.2 | `row[0]` is accessed without checking whether the query returned a row (`row` could be `None` if `order_id` doesn't exist), which would raise an unhandled `TypeError` deep in the function rather than a clear, named error at the boundary. | Validate: `if row is None: raise OrderNotFoundError(order_id)` immediately after the fetch. |
| 9 | review_target.py:13-14 | Reliability — float arithmetic for money | Coding-standards §3.2 (type system for correctness) | Monetary values are computed with raw `float` (`total * 0.9`), which is subject to floating-point rounding error — not appropriate for currency. | Use `Decimal` for all monetary calculations. |

### Architecture assessment

This is a single-file, single-function fixture with no layer boundaries at all — there is no core/infrastructure/handler split to audit for the Dependency Rule (§2.2), which is itself the most significant structural concern: business logic (discount calculation), infrastructure I/O (SQL, HTTP), and error handling are all fused into one function with no ports/adapters separation (§5). This is consistent with the fixture's stated purpose (planted violations A/B/C), but items #1, #2, #6, and #7 are real defects beyond the three the docstring calls out and should not be waved through just because the file is a synthetic benchmark input — if this pattern is ever copied into production code, the SQL injection alone is a critical vulnerability.
